briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Pain, Real Workarounds: Michigan Operators Adapt While Federal Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax keeps squeezing smaller operators, but a new Ann Arbor grand opening, a hospitality-forward Muskegon buildout, and a fresh repeal bill show the market still has fight and opportunity in it. Nationally, DEA just urged its own judge to move marijuana to Schedule III, Curaleaf's bid for Aurora signals big-money confidence, and psychedelics keep racking up FDA wins.

local.text: New Standard is opening a new Ann Arbor location this week, with <cite index="27-1">New Standard Ann Arbor offering giveaways and discounts on opening weekend Sept. 3-6</cite> — a fresh flag planted in one of the state's most competitive retail corridors right as the industry looks for good news.

Fields Cannary's Muskegon project is pushing the retail format forward: <cite index="64-3">a hospitality-forward buildout in Muskegon that pushes the format further than most Michigan dispensaries have gone</cite>, with <cite index="64-10">Fields Cannary targeting a fall opening for its retail cannabis dispensary, with a full-service restaurant to follow</cite>.

Score one for operators against surveillance overreach: <cite index="64-8">Jars Cannabis wins removal of Madison Heights Flock camera</cite>, a small but real win for retailers pushing back on aggressive license-plate tracking near their stores.

Relief efforts are gaining traction on two fronts: <cite index="7-1">a Republican state representative introduced House Bill 6224 to repeal the 24% wholesale tax, characterizing it as an unnecessary burden on the industry</cite>, while gubernatorial candidate Chris Swanson keeps hammering the issue on the trail, warning that <cite index="22-1">excessive taxation drives consumers back to the illicit market and shrinks the legal one</cite>.

The tax is real pain, but there's a playbook emerging: while <cite index="7-12">Higher Love, a U.P.-based dispensary chain, closed five of its nine Upper Michigan locations, with company president Joni Moore attributing the closures entirely to the tax increase</cite>, rival <cite index="7-14">Rize, which operates three Upper Michigan locations, has managed to sustain growth by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements with suppliers, splitting the tax burden rather than absorbing it alone</cite>.

national.text: Cannabis M&A just moved up a weight class: <cite index="64-15,64-16">August 2026 cannabis M&A moved into a different weight class, as Curaleaf announced a US$4 per share takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis on August 10</cite> — a signal big operators still see growth ahead.

The federal rescheduling case is moving: <cite index="41-1">the DEA is formally urging the judge overseeing the federal marijuana rescheduling case to recommend moving marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III, arguing the evidence shows the drug no longer meets the requirements for the nation's most restrictive drug category</cite>, and <cite index="38-2">the full official transcript of the hearing has now been made available to the public</cite>.

FDA keeps clearing runway for psychedelic medicine: the agency finalized <cite index="52-5">its final guidance for industry, "Psychedelic Drugs: Considerations for Clinical Investigations," finalizing the 2023 draft</cite>, and has scheduled <cite index="52-6">a public hearing on the potential future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs for September 14, 2026</cite>.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy keeps delivering: six-month data showed <cite index="48-5">39% of patients achieving a clinically meaningful response after two doses of psilocybin – an effect maintained for an average of six months</cite>, with <cite index="48-1">commercial launch-readiness on track for end of 2026, with launch expected in first half of 2027</cite>.

Banking access keeps inching forward: <cite index="55-1">Sen. Jeff Merkley and others have once again reintroduced cannabis banking reform, this time in new waters – following the rescheduling of medical cannabis</cite>, while fintech Safe Harbor says it has <cite index="59-2">assisted in the processing of more than $36 billion in cannabis-related depository funds across 41 states and territories</cite>.
